newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Gov ponders resurrecting bond plan this fall.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Gov ponders resurrecting bond plan this fall.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar may try again this fall to push a general obligation bond program through the General Assembly, his spokesman said Friday.
Mike Lawrence said the governor met with Republican legislative leaders Thursday to discuss the agenda for the fall veto session, which begins Nov. 19.

Lawrence said while no resolution was reached on the agenda, the governor discussed the possibility of third try at getting more bonding authorization passed. While no exact amount of bonding authority was discussed, Lawrence said it would probably equal the $590 million package for prisons and other projects that Edgar, a Republican, proposed in March.
For the past two years, the governor has been thwarted by Democratic legislators in getting the necessary three-fifths vote for bonding approval.

Lawrence pointed out that House Minority Leader Michael Madigan said in September he would support some debt issuance for prisons. Madigan is in line to become the new speaker of the Illinois House in January after his party won a slim majority in Tuesday's election.

Republicans, who currently control both chambers, may use the veto session to push through several proposals, including a state takeover of Meigs Field, a small airport on Chicago's downtown lakefront.
Lawrence said legislation for the airport, which Chicago Mayor Richard Daley has closed in anticipation of turning it into a bond-financed nature park, was discussed with Republican leaders.
Another possibility for the fall session is an adivsory referendum on school funding, Lawrence added.

Edgar was unsuccessful in his attempt last spring to get lawmakers to place a constitutional amendment on the ballot that would require the state to pay at least 50 percent of education costs in exchange for lower local property taxes.
Mike Cys, a spokesman for House Speaker Lee Daniels, R-Elmhurst, said the Republicans' agenda may be finalized next week.
A spokesman for Madigan was not available to comment.
